title: Expression and Comprehension

examples: First we eat, then we play, last we sleep.
First the bird came, then it ate, last it flew away.
I feel happy because we played.
I feel sad because my toy broke.
I feel proud because I read a book.
A car is bigger than a bike.
I run faster than my friend.

patterns.text: The story: ___ retold in three sentences
examples: Here is my story. A dog found a ball. Then it lost it. Last a girl gave it back.
Can I have the ball, please?
You like the park? What do you play there?
You drew a car? What color is it?

exits: Child retells a story using first, next, then, final words.
Child carries an eight-to-ten-turn two-way conversation on a familiar topic.
Child answers literal and prediction questions about a spoken story.

activities.title: Story chain
activities.how: Start a story sentence, the child adds the next, and you alternate three or four times, then have the child retell the whole chain.

activities.title: Feelings guess
activities.how: Describe a small situation and have the child name the feeling with a because reason, then invent one for you.

activities.title: Shop role-play
activities.how: Run a polite shop exchange where the child asks with Can I have ___, please? and thanks you; then swap roles.

assessment.ask: Have the child retell three steps of a routine with first, then, last.
Have the child say how they feel and why with I feel ___ because ___.
Have the child compare two familiar things with bigger than or the biggest.
Tell a four-sentence story, then have the child retell it in three sentences.
Have the child ask for something politely and respond politely to you.
Tell the child one thing about you and have them ask a follow-up question.
Have the child ask you three different question-word questions.
Talk about today and tomorrow and have the child use both time words correctly.
Have the child describe two emotions with a situation for each.
Have the child read four two-syllable words aloud: tiger, water, rabbit, under.

goals: Describe a feeling with a reason.
Show confidence by speaking at length without prompting.
Show curiosity by asking about words and ideas.
Encourage patience while building a longer answer.
checkin: Ask how the child feels today and have them add a short reason.
Ask what kind of day it has been, using one feeling word and one reason.
Ask what the child is looking forward to today.
praise: You told that in the right order.
You gave a reason for your feeling.
You carried the whole answer on your own.
You listened and answered the exact question.
You kept trying after a tricky word.
You used a word from an earlier lesson.
You corrected yourself and kept speaking.
You remembered what you practiced before.
encourage: It is fine to think before you answer.
Every mistake teaches us the next step.
You do not have to be fast to be good.
Long answers are built one sentence at a time.

calm.title: Balloon breathing
calm.how: Guide one slow balloon breath: in while lifting the arms, out slowly. Then name one easy sentence to say together.

calm.title: Two good things
calm.how: Ask for two good things about today, then turn one of them into a simple sentence together.

calm.title: Slow story
calm.how: Tell a short calm story with no questions, then have the child tell one line of it back.
